newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CORTECS SAYS PSEUDOSTAT TESTS POSITIVE.
newsitem.headline: CORTECS SAYS PSEUDOSTAT TESTS POSITIVE.

text.p: Drug development group Cortecs International Ltd said on Tuesday it had positive results for the completed Phase II trial of its oral therapeutic vaccine Pseudostat in patients with chronic bronchitis.

The objective of the trial was to demonstrate clinical efficacy in chronic bronchitis patients, who have a history of two or more acute infective exacerbations per year, Cortecs said. "Today's results dictate that we now proceed into our planned Phase III programmes in chronic bronchitis and bronchiectasis," president Michael Flynn said in a statement.
Cortecs said 91 patients were recruited to take part in the double-blind, placebo-controlled study. The patients received a Pseudostat oral immunisation course.

During the five months following completion of immunisation the number of acute infective episodes in the placebo group was about 10 times higher than in the Pseudostat group, whereas up to completion of immunisation the infection rate had been similar in the two groups, Cortecs said.
Flynn said Cortecs also planned to begin our Phase II European cystic fibrosis clinical programme very soon.

Chronic bronchitis is a disease characterised by persistent underlying lung infection and causing 28 million lost working days and five percent of deaths per year in Britain alone, Cortecs said. Worldwide it is estimated that more than five million people suffer from the disease, the company said.

The disease is characterised by intermittent acute episodes of infection which, unless treated promptly, may lead to further damage to the lungs and a worsening of the underlying chronic bronchitis, it said. Cortecs is a British-based company quoted on the London and Australian stock exchanges and on Nasdaq. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
